questions.knowledge_point: Using Alternative Forms of Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions
questions.problem: Express $2{cos}^{2}⁡{22}^{∘}-1$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={22}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{cos}^{2}⁡{22}^{∘}-1 & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2\cdot {22}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{44}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Express $1-2{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={15}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{15}^{∘} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {15}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:

$$
1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={75}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2{sin}^{2}⁡({75}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {75}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{5\pi }{12}) & =cos\,(2\cdot \frac{5\pi }{12}) \\  & =cos\,(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that our expression is a perfect square that can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{4}\,(\frac{\pi }{4})-2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}){sin}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4})+{sin}^{4}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={({cos}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}))}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =cos\,(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =cos\,(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{({cos}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{\pi }{4}))}^{2} & ={0}^{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$
